title: block content
description: The `content` object of a block (`type: 'bento'`, the fixed discriminator): an optional stem, a list of tiles on the 12-column grid, and an optional beat timeline. Generated from the runtime validator — regenerate rather than edit. Prose documentation: blocks/bento.md.

stem.description: An optional line of text above the grid that frames the block, such as the stem of a question. Figures belong in tiles, not here.

id.description: An id unique within the block. Beats and dialogue turns refer to a tile by it.

part.description: Groups tiles into the lettered or numbered parts of a question: a lowercase letter or roman numeral. Surfaces render the part label from this field, so the tile text does not repeat it. A part's tiles are contiguous in the list.

speaker.description: The id of a speaker in a dialogue tile of this block. The tile is shown as that speaker's, with their avatar beside it and no speech bubble.

col.description: The leftmost column, counting from 1 of 12.

row.description: The top band, counting from 1. Bands are unbounded; a slide shows six, and a taller block paginates at band boundaries.

w.description: The width in columns. Spans of 3, 4, 6 and 12 are a quarter, a third, a half and the full width.

h.description: The height in bands, at most 6, so that a tile fits one slide.

cell.description: The rectangle the tile occupies on the 12-column grid. Tiles do not overlap; empty cells are allowed.

intent.description: For LaTeX keys only: "equivalent" accepts any algebraically equal form; "same-form" compares the written form.

groups.description: Constraints across several typed answers. A group of blanks with anyOrder is marked by one-to-one assignment, so either order is accepted; distinct requires the entries to differ; sum requires them to total the given number. A group of pairs lists ordered tuples of blank ids and is marked tuple by tuple. A group carries blanks or pairs, not both.

marking.description: How the tile is scored. Mode "auto" carries a machine-checked key and sits on an options, matching, ordering, gaps, table or model tile. Mode "rubric" carries a scheme a person marks against and sits on a text or working tile that states the task. Mode "none" is unmarked. A marked tile's block declares role "question" or "worked-example". Answers are stored against the block id and tile id.

kind.description: "free-text" gives ruled prose lines; "working" gives squared space for stepped mathematics.

lines.description: The size of the answer space in lines. When omitted, two lines per rubric mark, between 4 and 12.

response.description: The answer space of a rubric-marked tile: an input on the web, ruled lines or working space in print and in Word export. Nothing marks what is written here by machine.

responseMode.description: For a marked model tile: how the answer is given on the figure. Each mode names an interaction and what the key is. place-point: a point is placed; the key is coordinates. select-point: a drawn point is chosen; the key is its label. select-region: an area is chosen; the key is a set of region ids. run-value: the model reports a computed value; the key is a value. run-sheet, run-program, run-query and run-figure: the model runs what was written and marks the result; the key is derived from the model's parameters. fill-derived, place-derived and construct: hidden values are typed, placed or shaped and checked against what the model derives from its own data. place-line, show-inequality, mark-cross, plot-curve, transform-curve, sketch-curve, draw-histogram and draw-tangent: a line, interval, cross, curve, bar or tangent is drawn or moved into place and checked against the target named in the model's parameters. For every derived mode the key is { derived: true } and the model's parameters carry the target. The model must list the mode among those it supports.

text.description: Prose: paragraphs and lists as a rich-text document.

working.description: Stepped written mathematics: equation chains, elimination, proofs with reasons, the balance method. Lines are aligned on their relation automatically from plain equations. Annotations are optional and used sparingly.

lhsAlign.description: How the left-hand side of each line is aligned. "right" (the default) suits equation chains; "left" suits balance-method layouts.

statement.description: The line: one paragraph of text and mathematics. A mathematical line is usually a single math node.

label.description: A short lead-in in the gutter, for equation references and operation notes. Parenthesised integers such as "(1)" render as circled references; notes such as "×100" render as written.

note.description: A reason shown in a right-hand column, smaller and muted; it may contain mathematics.

rule.description: A thick rule: "above" sits on a result line, as in column addition; "below" underlines the line.

align.description: Whether the line joins the relation alignment. Default true; false for prose lines and full-width givens.

alignAt.description: A manual alignment point, as a character offset into the statement, for the rare case where the derived alignment is wrong.

arcs.description: Arcs linking terms in the statement, as in an expansion. Each arc joins two term marks authored in the statement's LaTeX.

from.description: The mark id of the first term.

to.description: The mark id of the second term.

side.description: Whether the arc bows above or below the terms. Default above.

result.description: Answer lines: one LaTeX string per line, each shown centred on a dotted answer line beneath the working, revealed last.

ref.description: The pinned model reference, family/name@version, such as "graphing/coordinate-grid@4". Open Resource also resolves a "user:<id>" reference to a model published from its workshop; such references are not part of the public library.

params.description: The model's parameters, valid against the parameter schema of the version pinned by ref (models/<family>/<name>/<version>.json).

altText.description: A description of what the rendered figure shows, written from the parameters. It is the accessibility text, the text that search sees, and what is shown if the figure cannot render.

caption.description: An optional caption as a rich-text document, shown as a small line beneath the figure.

id.description: The stage's name in kebab case. Stage markers in a text document refer to a step by this id; beat ops refer to it by its zero-based index.

ref.description: Optionally, a different model for this stage, pinned like the slot's ref. When omitted the stage uses the slot's model.

params.description: The complete parameter set for this stage, not a patch, valid against the stage's model.

altText.description: An optional accessibility text for this stage. When omitted the slot's altText applies.

revealAt.description: For a figure on a question: the answer-reveal beat, counting from 1, at which this stage becomes active. Between pegged beats the figure holds. When no step carries revealAt, the figure completes on the final reveal.

steps.description: An optional staged progression of the figure: each entry is a complete parameter set reached in order after the base params, on the same model unless the step names its own ref. On a model tile a beat op of type "stage" advances to a step; in a staged text document, stage markers between top-level nodes advance it in step with the prose; on a question, steps advance with the answer reveal, each pegged to a beat by revealAt or, when none is pegged, completing on the final reveal.

model.description: A computed figure from the model library, in the position an image would take. It is generated from params rather than bound to an asset.

url.description: The video's URL: a YouTube or Vimeo link, a direct video file, or a video uploaded to Open Resource. The renderer chooses the player from the URL.

altText.description: A description of what the video shows or teaches. It is the accessibility text, the text that search sees, and what is shown where a video cannot play, as in print.

title.description: An optional short title shown above the player.

caption.description: An optional caption as a rich-text document, shown beneath the video, such as a source credit.

video.description: An embedded video from a URL, in the position an image would take.

speaker.description: The id of one of the tile's speakers.

about.description: Optionally, the id of another tile in the block this turn comments on; the bubble points at it.

dialogue.description: Speech between named speakers, each shown with an avatar, as ordered turns with one bubble per turn.

id.description: An optional cell id, required on the gap cells of an auto-marked table so that the key can name them.

gap.description: The cell's content is withheld. On a teaching surface a beat reveals it; on an auto-marked table the pupil types into it.

table.description: A rectangular grid of cells, every row the same length, with optional header row and column. With marking on the tile, gap cells become typed-answer inputs.

variant.description: "single" has one correct option, "multi" several, and "boolean" is a fixed true-or-false pair with no authored options.

feedback.description: A note on the item: for a distractor, why it tempts and where it goes wrong; for the right answer, why it is right. It is the record of the item's reasoning and is never shown to the pupil; the worked solution a pupil reads is the block's explanation.

misconceptionId.description: The id of the misconception in the resource's registry that this distractor embodies. Never shown to the pupil.

options.description: The options. Omitted for the boolean variant.

correctWhen.description: The truth value this justification is correct for.

justification.description: For the boolean variant: the secondary options that justify the answer.

options.description: A choice question. The key is one option id for "single", an array of ids for "multi", and a boolean for "boolean".

variant.description: "pairs" matches one to one between equal columns; "categorise" matches many left items to each right item.

ordering.description: An ordering question. The key is the item ids in the correct sequence.

input.description: "math" makes the blank a mathematics field whose key is a set of LaTeX forms compared structurally, so that notational variants match and a different mathematical form does not. Omitted for a plain typed blank.

intent.description: For mathematics blanks: "same-form" (the default) assesses the written form, so an unsimplified or rearranged answer is wrong; "equivalent" accepts any algebraically equal answer.

template.description: The cloze text, stored as an array of text runs and blanks.

gaps.description: A cloze: text with typed blanks. The key maps each blank id to a string, an array of accepted strings, a set key when one blank takes a collection, or a precision key when the written precision is assessed. A blank whose answer is mathematical notation declares input "math" and its key is a set of LaTeX forms compared structurally.

cols.description: A fixed column count. When omitted the grid balances itself.

ref.description: The pinned model reference, family/name@version, such as "graphing/coordinate-grid@4". Open Resource also resolves a "user:<id>" reference to a model published from its workshop; such references are not part of the public library.

primitive.description: A computed figure from the model library, in the position an image would take. It is generated from params rather than bound to an asset.

icon.description: An icon accent on the card, which may sit beside an image.

items.description: A uniform collection of cards, never marked. Beats can reveal one item at a time.

glossary.description: A list of terms and definitions, never marked.

items.description: One tile. Exactly one payload slot is set, and that slot is the tile's kind: text, working, image, model, video, dialogue, table, options, matching, ordering, gaps, items or glossary. Options, matching, ordering, gaps and table tiles may carry marking; items and glossary never do.

tile.description: The id of the tile the op targets.

op.description: "reveal" (the default) shows the target; "hide" removes it; "stage" advances a model to the step named by stage.

turn.description: For a dialogue tile: the zero-based turn. Omitted to target the whole tile.

paragraph.description: For a text tile: the zero-based paragraph. Omitted to target the whole tile.

line.description: For a working tile: the zero-based statement line. A tile-level op with no line reveals the rest of the working, including the result.

result.description: For a working tile: reveals the result box on its own.

stage.description: For a model tile with op "stage": the zero-based index into the model's steps.

tableRow.description: For a table tile: the zero-based row of the target cell, with tableCol.

tableCol.description: For a table tile: the zero-based column of the target cell, with tableRow.

item.description: For an items tile: the zero-based item, so that cards reveal one at a time. Omitted to target the whole tile. Options, ordering and matching tiles reveal as one.

answer.description: Marks the op as revealing an answer rather than pacing the teaching. Such ops are withheld on pupil-facing surfaces: behind "Show answer" in quiz mode and in the answers section of a printed workbook. A block in a sequence with an answer-flagged op is a posed question and carries role "question".

beats.description: The reveal timeline: an ordered list of beats, each a set of ops that happen together on one click. Anything an op targets starts hidden; everything else is visible from the start. Slides play the timeline; the web and print surfaces show it played through, with answer-flagged ops held back for the answers.

ids.description: The registry entry ids to render. When projection is omitted the whole registry renders.

projection.description: For a projection block (role objectives, glossary, assumed-knowledge, misconceptions or teacher-tips): an optional subset of the registry the block renders.

richTextDoc.description: A TipTap rich-text document — the shape every text field carries. Full shape: schemas/tiptap-doc-schema.json.
